opencode.label: OpenCode
opencode.invocation: Ask OpenCode to use reverse-engineering-investigator; its native skill tool loads the named skill. Verify it appears in the available-skill list. Do not assume a slash command with the skill name exists.
opencode.notes: OpenCode also discovers .agents/skills and Claude-compatible locations. Use one visible copy. Compaction, session resume and tool configuration remain OpenCode operations; use the installed version's exposed controls.

claude-code.label: Claude Code
claude-code.invocation: Use /reverse-engineering-investigator with the task, or ask Claude to use the skill. Verify that the command/skill is discovered in this workspace.
claude-code.notes: The project layout and personal layout differ in cloud availability: local personal skills are not automatically read by Claude Code cloud sessions. For a cloned project, include the project skill. Keep frontmatter portable; this package adds no allowed-tools policy, dynamic shell injection, hooks or context: fork requirement.

codex.label: Codex CLI / IDE
codex.invocation: Mention $reverse-engineering-investigator or select it through /skills in supported Codex CLI/IDE surfaces. Verify discovery in the current workspace.
codex.notes: These are external local Codex skill paths. ChatGPT's managed personal-skill installation is a separate distribution mechanism. Keep repository policies in their existing instruction mechanism; the exporter does not overwrite AGENTS.md. Do not infer available tool names, compaction APIs or background-job persistence from the Codex brand.

cursor.label: Cursor
cursor.invocation: Use /reverse-engineering-investigator or attach the skill with @ in Agent chat on a supporting version. Verify it is listed and the Agent reads SKILL.md.
cursor.notes: Cursor also discovers shared .agents/skills and compatibility directories. Prefer one copy. User skills and remote/cloud workers have different availability; include project skills in a shared workspace or use Cursor's documented sync controls when desired. This package does not generate always-applied rules or modify those controls.

antigravity.label: Antigravity 2.0 / IDE
antigravity.invocation: Ask Antigravity to use reverse-engineering-investigator; inspect active skills in the IDE Customizations menu. Antigravity 2.0 documents /reverse-engineering-investigator for manual invocation; verify the installed surface supports it.
antigravity.notes: Current documentation defaults to .agents/skills and keeps .agent/skills compatibility. Use the current layout for new installs. The 2.0 and standalone IDE global location is .gemini/config/skills; CLI uses a different global location. Do not turn skill instructions into legacy workflows or assume IDE tools exist in CLI.

antigravity-cli.label: Antigravity CLI
antigravity-cli.invocation: Use /reverse-engineering-investigator in the interactive CLI TUI after verifying skill discovery. The documentation describes conversion of skills into slash commands.
antigravity-cli.notes: CLI and IDE share the project skill layout but have different global locations and runtime capabilities. A skill export is not an Antigravity plugin installation. Keep existing plugin, permission and model configuration under host control.

pi.label: Pi
pi.invocation: Use /skill:reverse-engineering-investigator followed by the task. Inspect startup diagnostics; /reload refreshes skills after editing in an active session.
pi.notes: This adapter uses Pi's documented shared Agent Skills locations. Preserve the directory form and relative supporting files. Name collisions keep the first discovered skill, so remove duplicate visible versions. Subagents/extensions are optional host capabilities, not prerequisites of this skill.

shared.label: Shared Agent Skills
shared.invocation: Use the installed host's skill invocation; verify its discovery path.
shared.notes: Suitable for documented shared-layout hosts; use Claude Code's native export separately.

generic.label: Generic explicit loader
generic.notes: No automatic discovery claim is made for an unfamiliar host.
